data.name: AION Aurelia system controller (DMA, banking and refresh)

dma.bank_selection: Latch physical source/destination bank and offsets on start. CPU mapping changes cannot redirect an active transfer; split logical buffers at 4 KiB boundaries before programming physical segments. Reject ROM writes, unmapped banks and out-of-range lengths.
dma.arbitration: Bounded bursts with guaranteed CPU and refresh service; device-ready/WAIT handshake; video uploads yield to video-controller fetch deadlines. Numeric grant limits require cycle-level validation.
dma.completion: Completion/error interrupt, readable remaining count, controlled abort; reset disables DMA.
dma.video_endpoint: Auto-incrementing upload ports for display DRAM or dedicated sprite SRAM; target-ready backpressure.
dma.peripheral_scope: Disk/FlexiBUS DMA requires qualified request/ready or FIFO endpoints and drivers; legacy programmed I/O remains supported.

refresh.scope: System DRAM only, including hidden banks and expansion. Video controller refreshes display DRAM; sprite SRAM needs no refresh.
refresh.scheduler: Always-running timer, row counter and refresh arbitration during CPU execution, HALT and DMA; initialize before enabling RAM use. Match row count and retention deadlines to each qualified system DRAM type.
supported_populations: 48 KiB: three banks of eight 16Kx1 DRAMs
64 KiB expanded Aurelia: four banks of eight 16Kx1 DRAMs
64 KiB Aurelia+: one bank of eight 64Kx1 DRAMs

specification.bank_control: 0000–6FFF fixed lower RAM; 7000–EFFF switchable in 4 KiB pages; F000–FFFF common RAM. Boot ROM at zero until normal-map release.

manufacturing_planning.status: 3 micron planning estimate; pin count, layout, timing and speed-bin yield pending

manufacturing_requirements: Qualify CPU bus handover at 4 and 6 MHz, bounded DMA bursts, device-ready waits, completion interrupts and abort/reset recovery.
Verify independent refresh for every installed physical bank, including hidden banks and Aurelia 16 KiB expansion; derive deadlines from qualified DRAM ordering codes.
Freeze package/pinout, external buffers, memory decode, bank-latched DMA addressing and simultaneous video/peripheral stress tests.
